title: Building on Working Relationship with Saudi Authorities to Manage Haj Arrangements and Quotas for Singaporeans
what_it_is: Building on Working Relationship with Saudi Authorities to Manage Haj Arrangements and Quotas for Singaporeans

sections.label: Singapore Haj quota and arrangements
sections.summary: Singapore has 900 Haj places, requested more from Saudi Arabia, uses a MUIS queue with priority for pilgrims aged 70 and above, and faces new health certificate rules from 2026.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: asked the Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs how Singapore builds on its established working relationship with the Saudi authorities in managing Haj arrangements, including addressing considerations around (i) quota allocation, (ii) queue arrangements and (iii) health requirements for senior pilgrims.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We have a quota of 900 places for Haj pilgrims from Singapore and have requested for more Haj places.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Most recently, I conveyed this request to the Minister of Hajj and Umrah, Dr Taufiq bin Fawzan Al-Rabiah, during my visit to Saudi Arabia in November 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The Islamic Religious Council of Singapore (MUIS) administers our Haj quota through the MyHajSG portal queue system.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: An exception is made for senior Haj pilgrims, aged 70 years and above, who are given priority consideration.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: From 2026, Saudi Arabia will introduce new requirements for Haj pilgrims to produce a valid medical health certificate.

sections.label: Saudi Haj quota formula
sections.summary: Saudi Arabia sets each country's Haj quota at 0.1% of its Muslim population, giving Singapore 900 places for Haj 2026, while Singapore requests additional quota.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: If you look at how the system works today, Saudi Arabia sets the Haj quota for various countries based on a standardised formula, that is 0.1% of each country's Muslim population.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: So, Singapore was allocated 900 places for Haj 2026.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Having said that, over the years, if you look back and up to today, Singapore has proactively engaged Saudi Arabia to request for additional Haj quota.
